title: Real running-handle conformance, lease authority and same-run recovery source for the unique channel
statement: Three continuous engineering packages, nine outcomes. The unique channel now has (1) a pure conformance guard for the object runtime.launch returns (handle/producer/registration/callbacks validated before any endpoint is touched), (2) per-intent guard decisions with no cached approval, (3) a read-only lease-ownership predicate for control admission, (4) takeover/terminal semantics through main's real attach caller, (5) cross-kind id namespace plus journal-descriptor/payload-body coexistence, (6) bounded capacity/control behaviour at product scope, (7) the Runner journal as the same-run recovery source with no duplicated effect, (8) four-slot channel isolation and a clean reopen, (9) adoption/handoff material. The channel module itself is unchanged; the additions are a new guard module and one read-only adapter projection. Real launch-returned handles (native spawn), original Application/QuestionBroker recovery to candidate/accept, original scheduler 2/4 resource release and installed bytes remain NOT_REACHED.

additionsThisWave: running-attempt.ts: inspectRunningAttempt(running, expectation?) -> typed refusal before any socket/bind
attach.ts: RunnerAttachChannel.owns(connectionId, producer?) read-only ownership projection (no bind/poll/state copy)

outcomes.title: Real RunningAttempt-shaped handle and original three callbacks
outcomes.implementation: inspectRunningAttempt validates handle attemptId == producer attempt, full AttemptRef tuple, registration identity and the three callbacks before any endpoint use; main's attachRunnerAttempt consumes the validated port/callbacks
outcomes.positive: matching launch-shaped handle admitted; real service callbacks reach the original Store (row seq), the original payload body and one guard decision per intent
outcomes.negative: not-an-object/empty id/no port/incomplete registration/incomplete attempt/mismatched handle/missing callbacks/foreign binding refused with bounded messages; the same endpoint stays reachable for the real producer, so the refusal is identity not connectivity
outcomes.notReached: a handle actually returned by runtime.launch() (requires a native spawn, prohibited this wave); Application-created Work/QuestionBroker

outcomes.title: Fresh guard: per-intent decisions, no cached approval, ordered current
outcomes.implementation: original nativeWriteDecision wrapper over beforeNativeWrite; deny does not poison a command, allow is consumed once, current is evaluated at decision time
outcomes.positive: denied → allowed (after a live admission between intents) → consumed; a denial before the admission check does not consume it
outcomes.negative: after consumption the same command is refused; a later current flip refuses the next intent and only the next intent
outcomes.notReached: vendor/native effect observation; 30s channel timeout is not shortened (module-level timeout tests already cover it)

outcomes.title: First lease, legacy RPC and original command authority
outcomes.implementation: RunnerAttachChannel.owns() reports owned/unbound/stale_connection/identity_mismatch/closed without binding or polling; reference control consumer claims → owns → effect
outcomes.positive: legal CAS takes the next generation; owns() reports the live owner; a control path with the predicate allows exactly the owner
outcomes.negative: foreign producer refused and changes no owner; mismatched CAS refused and generation unchanged; terminal refuses new polls; never-bound/foreign lease claims refused with zero business effect
outcomes.notReached: B's runner-service controlRefusal still accepts a never-bound claimed lease before its own cache is set (B35-FIRST-CLAIMED-LEASE-IS-NOT-VALIDATED). I supplies the predicate and a reference integration; B must call it before command/cancel effects. Mixed-version cancel envelope remains B-owned.

outcomes.title: Temporary detach vs terminal through two real attach consumers
outcomes.implementation: replaced lease settles the pending write as indeterminate and requeues fact/payload work with original ids for the successor; terminal closes every lease
outcomes.positive: successor continues the same run, one Store receipt per fact in Store order, fresh intent decided by the current guard
outcomes.negative: pending write reported indeterminate (not allowed/denied); old generation cannot rebind (generation unchanged); terminal refuses the next poll
outcomes.notReached: same original Work recovery to check/currentCandidate/manualaccept; physical child stop

outcomes.title: Original ids, kind namespace, journal descriptor and payload body
outcomes.implementation: kind-namespaced correlation (fact:/payload:/write:) plus separate module maps; journal descriptor page vs immutable payload callback
outcomes.positive: fact payload-1 and payload request payload-1 settle concurrently and independently; 300-ref payload goes by reference, chunk bytes reproduce the descriptor digest and equal the callback body
outcomes.negative: duplicate receipt/payload replies refused (stale_lease); paging after the reported seq does not return the fact again; no settled request is redelivered
outcomes.notReached: payload chunking is read through main's existing /v1/payload; no new wire version

outcomes.title: Bounded capacity, control availability and honest diagnostics
outcomes.implementation: module bounds unchanged; write capacity refused before send; fact flow stays one-at-a-time through the real Runner
outcomes.positive: 65-fact flow produces 65 unique monotonically increasing receipts and a payload read interleaved at fact 10; 9 concurrent intents → 8 guard decisions + 1 capacity refusal, then capacity returns
outcomes.negative: capacity refusal is typed `capacity`; denied intents are `NativeWriteDenied`; after the burst the next intent is decided again
outcomes.notReached: fact saturation (64 pending) is not reachable through the product fact path because the Runner awaits each receipt; the refusal-before-send bound for facts is proven at module scope in concurrency.test.ts and is reported as such, not as a product-scope observation

outcomes.title: Same-run recovery source without a second ledger
outcomes.implementation: the Runner's own journal is the recovery source; the channel requeues only unsettled work; the Store stays the single receipt authority
outcomes.positive: after takeover the journal page names the original fact once with its own durable seq; the successor persists the next fact; Store rows unchanged
outcomes.negative: pending intent becomes indeterminate, migrates no approval (a later direct decision is denied), and does not become a command result; paging past the seq does not replay the fact
outcomes.notReached: original Application/QuestionBroker question/answer/native_applied, recovered candidate, explicit manualaccept, slot release

outcomes.title: Slot isolation and a clean reopen
outcomes.implementation: four independent services/endpoints/queues/leases; one lease cannot settle another slot; terminal channel closed; fresh Runner starts unbound
outcomes.positive: each slot persists only its own fact; closing slot 2 leaves 0/1/3 serving; a fresh Runner binds generation 1 → 2 with an empty page
outcomes.negative: cross-slot reply refused; terminal refuses the next poll; no ghost request in the fresh channel
outcomes.notReached: original scheduler 2/4-slot capacity, fifth-item waiting, UNKNOWN occupancy and barrier-driven release (original core/queue/bindings); archive/non-empty state migration is main/B/D scope

outcomes.title: Adoption manual, exact source and handoff
outcomes.implementation: docs/runtime-channel README + adoption manual updated with the real running shape, the identity guard, owns() and the layering rules; this status file separates source/controlled/installed/native/recovered/value
outcomes.consumer: this file plus the eight new test files and the two updated docs
outcomes.positive: call graph, authority ownership and error handling documented from the actual source
outcomes.negative: explicit NOT_REACHED list; no claim that module green equals product recovery
outcomes.notReached: installed exact package (D freeze → E final), native/vendor effects, value/benefit measurement

handoff.detail: B35-FIRST-CLAIMED-LEASE-IS-NOT-VALIDATED is unchanged in B source. RunnerAttachChannel.owns(leaseId, producer) is now the read-only predicate to call before command/cancel effects; the reference consumer in actual-lease-authority.test.ts shows the claim→owns→effect order with zero effect on refusal.

B35-ATTACH-HANDLE-IDENTITY-NOT-MATCHED is unchanged in packages/execution/src/attached-attempt.ts. inspectRunningAttempt (apps/runner/src/attach-channel/running-attempt.ts) is the pure validator consumers can run first; it refuses handle.attemptId != producer.attempt.attemptId before any endpoint is opened.

handoff.item: Client channel arity vs port interface
handoff.detail: packages/execution/src/recovery-transport.ts declares RecoveryRunnerPort.channelNext(producer, leaseId, expectedGeneration) for the server side, while connectRunnerRecovery()'s returned client takes (leaseId, expectedGeneration). A caller following the port type passes the producer as the lease and gets `invalid_lease`. Observed while writing actual-lease-authority.test.ts; documented with the runtime shape in that file. Needs a typed client interface so consumers cannot pass the wrong argument order.

An attach consumer must bind (first channelNext) before business feed starts: a native intent that exists while the stdio lease is still current is settled indeterminate by the takeover, which is correct but surprising. Observed and documented in actual-guard-decisions.test.ts.
